style: Say warmly with a gravelly voice, like an old shop teacher at a workbench.
lines: Four groups built magnets and got very different counts. Tap two group rows to see what they did differently.
Tap Add question to put that difference on your board.
Tap a question on the board, then change only that setting and tap Test.
Three trials, so one odd count can't fool you. Watch the nail tip.
Keep the other settings the same. Step this one through its values, one Test each.
These counts are all about the same. Try a stronger setup, then test again.
You have enough data. Tap Answer on the question.
Tap the sentence your chart supports. You get one try.
Right.
Not quite.
Now look at the numbers. Tap the answer closest to your own means.
Question tested.
The wire is warming up. Switch off between tests.
You changed a setting, so that test stopped. Tap Test.
Balloon A lifted more bits with less rubbing. Tap both balloon rows to see why.
Drag the compass around the coil with the switch off. Watch the red end.
Points north.
It turned, and nothing touched it.
Back to north.
It turned around.
Same pattern, but the needle flipped. Tap the reason why.
Sam ran three tests, and each one has a flaw. Tap what's wrong with the first.
Tap Run it the fair way to see what Sam should have found.
Tap Next case.
Turn Switch on. Drag the compass near the coil.
Turn Switch off, then drag the compass around the coil. Watch the red end.
Turn Switch off while the needle is turned. Watch where it goes.
Switch on. Sprinkle filings, then tap Flip batteries.
Tap Sprinkle filings before and after Flip batteries. Compare the shape and the red end.
The turn is small. Choose Steel nail or more Turns and Batteries, then flip again.
The turn is small. Tap Coil settings for a stronger setup, then flip again.
The turn is small. Choose Steel nail or more Turns and Batteries, then move the compass nearby.
The turn is small. Tap Coil settings for a stronger setup, then move the compass nearby.
Drag the compass to map more places. Tap Drop arrow to leave a record on the paper.
These counts are too small to compare. Make a stronger fair set, then tap Answer again.
Tap a case number to revisit the evidence, or use another bench. Your first choices stay marked.
